stem: A client is medically stable for discharge and understands the medication plan but has unstable housing and unreliable transportation to follow-up visits. Which interpretation best explains why these barriers remain clinically relevant?

options.A: Address the housing issue only if it directly prevents medication storage, while treating transportation mainly as a scheduling inconvenience.
options.B: Recognize both as social determinants of health that can affect access to care and health outcomes after discharge.
options.C: Classify both barriers primarily as health-literacy problems even though the client understands the written plan.
options.D: Treat the barriers mainly as payer-authorization issues rather than factors that can affect the client's ability to carry out the discharge plan.

rationale: Healthy People 2030 defines social determinants of health as conditions in the environments where people live and identifies safe housing and transportation as examples. Its access-to-health-services literature summary states that unreliable transportation can interfere with consistent access to care and may contribute to negative health outcomes, while its housing-instability summary explains that unstable housing can negatively affect health and make healthcare access more difficult. These barriers therefore remain clinically relevant even when the client understands the medication instructions.
educational_objective: Recognize housing instability and transportation barriers as social determinants that can limit healthcare access and affect outcomes during discharge planning.

source_original.stem: A client is medically stable for discharge and understands the medication plan but has unstable housing and unreliable transportation to follow-up visits. Which interpretation best explains why these barriers remain clinically relevant?

options.A: Address the housing issue if it interferes with medication storage, while treating transportation mainly as a scheduling inconvenience.
options.B: Recognize them as social determinants that can limit access to care and influence outcomes after discharge.
options.C: Classify them mainly as health-literacy problems even though the client understands the written plan.
options.D: Refer them to financial counseling because their main clinical relevance is whether follow-up services can be authorized.

source_original.rationale: Healthy People 2030 identifies housing and transportation as social determinants of health and notes that transportation barriers can interfere with access to care and worsen outcomes. Therefore, option B best explains why the barriers belong in discharge planning even when the client understands the instructions. Option A incorrectly waits for a direct complication and minimizes transportation as merely scheduling. Option C misclassifies access barriers as health-literacy problems despite the client understanding the plan. Option D confuses social determinants with utilization management and payer authorization.
source_original.source_detail: HHS ODPHP Healthy People 2030 — Social Determinants of Health: housing and transportation are SDOH; transportation barriers can limit access to care and influence health outcomes. Healthy People 2030 current federal framework; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; Assignment, Delegation and Supervision; prioritization/continuity/client rights as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the construct and key. Rewrote distractors A and D to remove overly narrow or administrative framing and verified housing and transportation claims separately against current Healthy People 2030 literature summaries. Recalibrated difficulty from hard to medium because the item tests recognition of a well-defined discharge-planning concept.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Discharge planning — social determinants of health
audit_findings.source_authority: Current federal HHS ODPHP Healthy People 2030 framework and literature summaries.
audit_findings.currentness: Healthy People 2030 remains the current federal framework and pages were rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: General SDOH page supports housing/transportation classification; separate access and housing-instability summaries support downstream access/outcome relevance.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final wording uses 'can'/'may' rather than converting associations into deterministic outcomes.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrectly minimizes transportation and makes housing relevance contingent on one specific mechanism.
distractor_audit.B: Uniquely integrates both barriers as SDOH with healthcare-access/outcome relevance.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because the stem explicitly establishes understanding of the plan; access barriers are not synonymous with health literacy.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrectly narrows the barriers to payer authorization instead of execution/access of the discharge plan.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B correctly explains the clinical relevance of both barriers.
audit_findings.cueing: All options remain discharge-planning interpretations rather than unrelated facts.
audit_findings.blueprint: Maps to Management of Care continuity/referrals/resource coordination.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Adversarial review verified that housing instability and unreliable transportation are each independently supported and avoided causal overstatement.
